title: A Multi-Instance Coordinator Document holds the strategy that no single Instance can express
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2 introduces the Multi-Instance Coordinator Document: it "provide[s] general specifications of the Spark Liquidity Layer and define[s] Spark's overarching strategy and operational framework for managing **across all Instances**."

This is the necessary counterpart to per-Instance configuration. Granular Instances give precise control over each exposure, but they cannot express anything about the portfolio: concentration across venues, how much total capital is deployed, which chain gets liquidity when several want it. Those are properties of the set, not of any member.

So the Artifact adds a document type one level up. The Coordinator holds the shared infrastructure — the Allocator and ALM contract addresses, the operational roles, the off-chain parameters — and the strategy that governs how Instances are used together.

The design lesson generalizes beyond Spark: any system that decomposes a portfolio into independently configured units needs an explicit home for cross-unit policy, or the aggregate behaviour becomes an emergent side effect of many local decisions that no document describes. The Coordinator is where the Liquidity Layer stops being a list of positions and becomes a strategy.
description: Because allocation is configured one chain-venue-asset triple at a time, the Artifact needs a separate document for the overarching framework governing behaviour across all Instances.
